body: I haven't looked into details, but is it related to this change? https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/skylark/backward-compatibility.html#expand-directories-in-args

The behavior is the same even if you set expand_directory=True so the value of the default argument shouldn't be related.

Even so, would expect expand_directory=True to expand to multiple files and expand_directory=False to stay as the directory name. In neither case would I expect it to be nothing (unless the directory is actually empty).

issue.body:
### Description of the bug:


When you declare a directory and then attempt to use it in `ctx.actions.run`, it silently skips the argument.

### Which category does this issue belong to?


_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


https://github.com/matts1/bazel-base/tree/directory-repro

```
def my_rule(ctx):
  out = ctx.actions.declare_file("file")
  out_dir = ctx.actions.declare_directory("dir")
  args = ctx.actions.args()
  args.add_all([out, out_dir])
  ctx.actions.run(..., arguments=[args])
```

When you run with `bazel build -s`, you can see that the command it ends up invoking is `<binary> path/to/file` and it completely skips the directory argument.

Additionally, `print(args)` reveals that the args is generated correctly, but fails to translate correctly to the command-line.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


7.0.0

No - I was also able to repro on 6.0.0

issue.body:
…of inputs list in `Args.add_{all,joined}`

This is an analogue of b7590a03b48b353b72415a1896d014130740b535 for `TreeArtifact`s.

Previously, when users forgot to add a `TreeArtifact` (aka a "directory") to the inputs of an action, `Args` would silently expand the contents to the empty set and thus (usually) not add anything to the command line. This made the mistake difficult to track down.

Fixes #6487
